feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It is polished and readable, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, less repetition across skills sections, and more outcome-focused evidence beyond responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and technical breadth.  
- Strong domain positioning: digital platforms, governance, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently presented.  
- Good use of scale indicators and specifics (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which boosts credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes and business impact in each role, not just duties—e.g., traffic growth, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings, or adoption metrics.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation is inconsistent between sections; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent unless intentional; “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—prefer “French (A2, improving)” or similar.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground scope/scale: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Replace the generic “building the platforms” phrasing with stronger action language such as “leading modernization,” “scaling,” or “optimizing.”
- Consider adding one concrete signal of scale from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “multi-channel platforms serving millions annually.”
- Streamline the second sentence to group related capabilities: “Specializes in enterprise web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” and the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” are somewhat repetitive.
- The capability list closely mirrors Core Competencies; shorten here to avoid sounding like a second skills section.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline, but this block currently overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, cleaner phrases and keep the list focused on differentiators: enterprise web, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel digital communications” for clarity and smoother style.
- Consider tightening “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search experiences” unless content design is a major target role.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel digital communications • AI-enabled search experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid mirroring exact phrasing.
- “Public-sector communications” appears in the header, so pairing it with “advocacy” is enough without expanding further here.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: e.g., “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched,” “Produced.”
- Increase specificity where possible with scale or audience impact: users, content volume, campaign duration, conference/event context, or distribution reach.
- Tighten wording: “bill-level AI chat” may be clearer as “AI chat at the bill level”; “continued campaign growth” could become “future campaign expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work closely overlap with current/previous NACo bullets; this footer should emphasize distinct project outcomes or formats, not restate responsibilities.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most differentiated item; consider leading with it.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, strategic advisory value, and only the newest/highest-impact work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled member discovery experiences.”
- Collapse overlapping duties into 3–4 impact bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on improving cross-channel coordination and publishing efficiency.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/microsites launched, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/lift, publishing time reduced, stakeholder teams supported, traffic or engagement gains.
- Use stronger consultant phrasing: “Designed,” “launched,” “streamlined,” “advised,” “led,” instead of “consult,” “build,” “develop,” “deliver.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting” may feel too execution-heavy/redundant with prior NACo roles unless tied to a specific launch or result.
- The AI search and microsite work duplicates Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let the project section carry the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 impact bullets, prioritizing the Drupal migration, analytics buildout, and studio launch.
- Strengthen outcomes where possible: add % improvements, cost savings, production volume, engagement growth, reporting speed, or adoption by 50+ publishers.
- Suggested phrasing:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast video studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia production.
- Expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role.
- “Governance/publishing standards” may duplicate consultant work unless tied to specific outcomes here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but the item reads internally focused and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around execution leadership, audience reach, and systems/process improvements with clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scale: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial and advocacy communications.”
- Combine related bullets for concision: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders, strengthening recurring member engagement.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel.”
- Sharpen the operations bullet: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”  
  If possible, add metrics such as open rates, production volume, turnaround time, or audience growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video” and “workflow” themes repeat in both the prior and subsequent NACo roles; keep this version focused on building/operating the channel, not studio expansion or enterprise governance.
- Avoid repeating generic channel lists already covered in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, outcome-oriented positioning, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy & information architecture
- Use “content operations” or “platform modernization” to better reflect recent leadership work at NACo.
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets for punchier scanning and less repetition.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable detail for experience bullets rather than skills lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and partially redundant with editorial workflow/content strategy language.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work, not every platform detail.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-stack items here: cut jQuery unless it is still central to current work.
- Consider dropping SharePoint and Power Pages from Topline Skills unless they are important for target roles; keep them in “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, make impact more explicit: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites” or “enterprise CMS modernization” to align with the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; Topline Skills should stay strategic and selective.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating exact phrasing everywhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and executive-level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Lead with capability, not tools: group platforms after the strategic skill so this feels senior rather than tactical.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive/leadership dashboards” or “Executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- If accurate, strengthen with one impact cue: “Analytics infrastructure and decision-support reporting” or “Measurement frameworks for high-traffic public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Consider keeping Topline Skills strategic and leaving the full tool stack only in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more senior, systems-oriented, and tied to the in-house studio/build-out work from the most recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability cluster: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event technical direction”
- Replace “video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “broadcast-quality video production” or “end-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider adding one measurable cue if format allows: “Built and operated NACo’s first in-house video studio” or “supported recurring advocacy programming and event production.”
- Keep terminology consistent with the CV’s leadership tone; “technical direction” or “production systems” reads stronger than “editing” alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already evidenced in Work Experience, so don’t over-expand this section.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strategic relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector focus) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- Add light proficiency framing if space allows: **Drupal (migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- If you want more impact, replace the heading with **CMS & Web Platforms** and align wording to recent work: emphasize Drupal first given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Keep it concise; don’t expand into tools or coding here since those are covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider merging or differentiating.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and seniority: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group operational tools separately: “Technical implementation & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add outcome/context language elsewhere or in a parenthetical: e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight edge/serverless functions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versions; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills item [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); avoid repeating the exact phrasing
- GTM also connects to analytics infrastructure already covered in recent NACo roles, so keep this list concise rather than restating analytics themes

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize categories and stronger tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match your positioning.
- Drop lower-value/older PM tools unless central to recent work: Basecamp and Trello feel less relevant than Airtable/Power Automate/Jira.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie tools to outcomes instead of listing all here, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams overlap with general workplace familiarity and may add less value than automation/integration tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Given the CV’s recent emphasis on enterprise email operations, this item should signal scale and purpose, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional context instead of only tools: **newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign journeys, member communications**
- Stronger version: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp | Email newsletter operations, audience segmentation, automated journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating scale here unless you add a distinct capability angle.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific or function-specific, not both.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics points already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize methods and decision-making value, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Analytics, Testing & Reporting**
- Replace with a tighter mix of tools + capabilities: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Consider swapping generic **Dashboarding** for stronger phrasing like **Executive dashboards** or **Performance reporting**
- If accurate, add one higher-signal capability instead of a broad term: **Attribution**, **Funnel analysis**, **Tagging strategy**, or **Conversion optimization**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep one more strategic and one more tool-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid overloading this section with the same wording.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” production volume, or audience impact if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding in-house publishing capacity.”
- Tighten the management line: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate,” if accurate.
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as launching or initially producing the series.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo roles; specify what changed or improved here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the standout achievement. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media work, this item should emphasize the podcast launch and innovation/program support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique accomplishment: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities at NACo.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider a tighter final version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy work; produced digital and multimedia content and launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on firsts and innovation/research support.
- Avoid repeating generic “supporting organizational programs and policy work” language used elsewhere unless you can add a concrete result.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads a bit generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills and several work bullets. Make it more tool-specific and execution-focused, or trim it to avoid repeating broader multimedia claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
- Tighten content to: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream production workflows**
